title: One ordinary reload while the living driver accelerates and brakes
caption: MOVING HULL / SAME PHYSICAL CARTRIDGE / SOURCE HANDS
input_audit: One ordinary gun-sight LMB discharge at 0.5s. Ordinary driver input accelerates at 4.25-6.6s and brakes through opposite drive input at 6.6-7.7s. The b44 stationary baseline records Carry at 5/6s and Ram at 7s; these timings guide the input schedule but do not force a phase, speed, grip, vehicle pose or successful reload. The disclosed turret-local render-only witness changes no live player aim or crew state. Enemy return fire is held for animation diagnosis.
visual_acceptance: Confirm from actual state_samples that both Carry and Ram occur while speed_m_s exceeds 0.1; a successful final reload alone is insufficient. Preserve a failed overlap or stall receipt.
Inspect the 4.25-8s video interval and stills at 5/6/7s: one existing round must follow common hull motion with the same source identity, current source hand targets and hull-local ownership receipt.
Compare speed at 6s and 7s to confirm actual braking while reloading; do not infer movement from input commands alone.
Inspect current mechanism hand_error_m separately from cached pose_target_error_m, keeping one-second sampling limits explicit.
Reject visible separation, stretched limbs, floor penetration, lost source materials or clipped body/cartridge geometry; this witness does not certify collision safety.
After the ordinary close phase the loader should return toward his source periscope position. Parked crew must not retain drive-induced motion indefinitely.
limitations: This witnesses common hull-motion covariance during ordinary loading, not an intentionally forced rejected grip. The isolated rejected-proposal and legacy owner conversion cases belong to CPU regressions. Turret-relative rejection behavior, accessible loader-side racks and the existing basket/breech envelope are unchanged. Whole-body collision, finger grips and swept cartridge contact remain incomplete. State checks alone do not establish visual acceptance.
